references.text: The Letter to the Hebrews warns that a bitter root may grow up and cause trouble, a direct reference to the poisonous root that leads people away from God in Deuteronomy 29:18.
Jeremiah speaks of those who say 'peace' to those who despise the Lord's word, reflecting the false assurance 'I shall have peace' in Deuteronomy 29:18.
Ezekiel condemns those who say 'peace' when there is no peace, similar to the self-deceptive attitude in Deuteronomy 29:18.
The psalm describes Israel's people as walking according to their own heart's plans, reflecting the expression 'I will walk in the stubbornness of my heart' in Deuteronomy 29:18.
Jeremiah warns against following the stubbornness of one's evil heart, the same theme found in Deuteronomy 29:18.
Jeremiah describes the people as having abandoned God's law and followed the stubbornness of their hearts, parallel to the warning in Deuteronomy 29:18.
The following verses elaborate on the consequences of the attitude described in verse 18, where the Lord will not forgive anyone who thinks this way.
Amos describes a plant that turns poisonous, reflecting the image of the poisonous root in Deuteronomy 29:18.
